findings.text: A zero-amount transfer rewrites the owner record of any LDA
An attacker reserves unminted LDA IDs, so the owner cannot mint them
Redemption trusts the `_OWNERS_` record and not the real balance
Any caller can run the V0_5_6 reinitializer and take the admin role
A burned LDA ID keeps its old owner
Zero-amount transfers raise tier balances while the backfill is open

The tier list uses a different index base on mint and on burn: Code smells: the index comes from `_CURRENT_SUPPLY_` after the increment; a bulk mint writes every ID to one slot — `_TIER_ENUMERATION_` starts at index 1 and a bulk mint keeps only the last ID. No function reads the list today, so we found no direct loss.

Zero-amount transfers call the royalties hook with any from and to: Code smells: `beforeLdaTransfer(from, to, tierId)` runs for zero-amount transfers and for IDs that do not exist — Any caller can make the royalties hook see a transfer that did not happen. The royalties contract is not in the repository, so we did not prove a loss of royalty funds.

A redemption re-mints at a tier index that is already in use: Code smells: the burn does not lower `_CURRENT_SUPPLY_`, and the new mint writes at index `_CURRENT_SUPPLY_` — Each redemption overwrites a valid ID in `_TIER_ENUMERATION_`. No function reads the list today, so we found no direct loss.

A trade approval also gives the right to redeem extras: Code smells: `isApprovedForAll(tokenOwner, redeemer)` lets any transfer operator redeem; the version bump cancels open orders — An approved marketplace operator can redeem the extra of a holder. We did not see whether the extras contract sends the extra to `redeemer`.

A pause does not stop transfers, permits or redemptions: Code smells: `whenNotPaused` is only on owner functions; `_beforeTokenTransfer`, `permit` and `onExtraRedeemed` have no pause check — When the owner pauses the contract, users can still use the zero-amount transfer path. We did not confirm what the pause is meant to stop.

A spender that loses PERMIT_SPENDER_ROLE keeps its approvals: Code smells: the role is checked once in `permit`; `safeTransferFrom` checks only `isApprovedForAll` — A revoked spender can still transfer the LDAs of each holder that signed a permit to it. The harm needs a trusted spender that turns hostile.

The burn path treats supply minus one as the last tier index: Code smells: `lastLdaIndex = _CURRENT_SUPPLY_[tierId] - 1` while the mint path writes at `_CURRENT_SUPPLY_` — The swap-and-pop removes the wrong slot from `_TIER_ENUMERATION_`. No function reads the list today, so we found no direct loss.

The backfill overwrites tier balances while transfers stay live: Code smells: `setOwnedTokens` writes an off-chain snapshot; a sender with a zero tier balance skips the decrement; old list entries above the new length stay — A legacy holder who moves an LDA before the backfill lands is counted twice by `tierBalanceOf`. We did not check how the royalties contract

composeLDA_ID does not check the 112-bit width of the token number: Code smells: `tokenID` is a `uint128` but the layout gives it 112 bits; the parts are joined with `+` — A token number above 112 bits writes into the version bits. No internal caller passes such a value.
